Subject: Clarify deployment boundary expectations — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion and helped clarify the high-level security posture you're targeting. Per our chat I wanted to summarize the open questions so we can move you toward a clear recommendation (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem). I'm attaching a short checklist (redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx) that we use to map requirements to deployment options.

Quick recap of what I heard:
- Primary concern: PHI in repo + downstream analytics (must be treated as regulated data).
- Current infra: mix of cloud-hosted EHR extracts (S3) and an on-prem analytics cluster for de-id processing.
- Expected traffic: bursty inference from product (peaks ~200 req/s during day).

Open questions for you (concrete answers will help us recommend Dedicated vs Private VPC):
1) Data-at-rest location: will inference requests contain direct PHI (i.e., identifiers) or only de-identified tokens? If PHI is present, is it uploaded to S3 or routed through your on-prem network?
2) Key management: do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model I/O and logs?
3) Network egress: must all inference traffic remain inside your VPC with no public egress? Any IP allowlist requirements?
4) Audit & retention: what retention window do you require for request/response logs and audit trails? Does a write-only audit stream to your Splunk/ELK exist?
5) Certificate & penetration testing: do you need annual pentest reports or on-demand evidence?

If most answers are "yes" to 1–3 and audit retention >90 days, we typically recommend a Private VPC deployment (or on-prem package) to meet isolation and key control requirements. Dedicated capacity can work if keys and ingress restrictions can be satisfied and the workload tolerance for shared control plane is acceptable.

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the attached checklist and send back by EOD Thursday.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical sync (engineers + security) — suggested times: Thu 6/10 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 6/11 8:00–9:00 PT.

Attachment: redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Clarify deployment boundary expectations — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers inline below, and I'll attach our network diagram after this note.

1) Data-at-rest / PHI: Yes, some inference payloads will contain direct PHI until our de-id step completes. Currently those payloads land in a restricted S3 bucket under our account. We also have an on-prem cluster that pulls nightly extracts for analytics.
2) Key management: We prefer customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS); HSM not strictly required but acceptable.
3) Network egress: Critical — the inference calls must not egress to the public internet. We require private VPC peering or an equivalent private link. IP allowlist is OK but we'd prefer a peered/private link.
4) Audit & retention: We need 12 months retention for request logs; can forward logs into our SIEM (Splunk).
5) Pentest reports: SOC 2 Type II is required; annual pentest evidence is a big plus.

Given the above, my leaning is toward Private VPC (the VPC peering and KMS requirements are the priority). That said, if Redwood can guarantee no customer-data egress and provide the KMS integration with per-tenant keys, Dedicated with a private network overlay could be acceptable.

I'll attach a compact network diagram and our compliance checklist in the next email.

—Liam

Internal notes / next steps (looping you both so we have a single source of truth):

Summary of Liam's answers:
- PHI in payloads (S3) and on-prem nightly extracts — means we need strong isolation and KMS control.
- Requires private link / VPC peering and 12-month log retention to Splunk.
- SOC 2 Type II required.

Preliminary recommendation: Private VPC (Helios-managed VPC peering) looks like the default path. Key reasons: customer-managed KMS, no public egress, and ability to forward logs into their Splunk. Dedicated could be viable if we can guarantee private networking and KMS integration per-tenant, but that will require product + infra sign-off on whether our control plane still touches any plaintext data or metadata that they consider sensitive.

Action items for infra/security team (please triage):
- Confirm whether Redwood's Dedicated control plane ever sees unredacted request payloads or only metadata. (INF-942)
- Validate KMS flow for customer-managed keys in both Dedicated and Private VPC builds; note any HSM gaps.
- Confirm architecture for VPC peering vs PrivateLink (latency/cost implications).

I'll create an internal ticket with the attached network diagram once Liam sends it. Karthik: can you block 60 minutes for a technical SRE call (we should include one infra lead + one product security resource)?
